title: What’s the latest on UK university compliance?
summary_en: This week, The PIE held the inaugural Compliance Con, bringing together compliance experts from across the UK sector. As tightened BCA thresholds loom, editor Beth Kennedy unpacks key takeaways from the event.
author: The PIE News team
title_cn: What’s the latest on UK university compliance?

title: Amaral Cunha, Escola Eleva
summary_en: This week, The PIE sat down with Amaral Cunha, head of school at Escola Eleva, part of Inspired Education Group. We spoke about his career to date and education's power to transform communities.
author: The PIE News team

title: Alphabetti spaghetti and Australia’s international education policy problem
summary_en: Neil Fitzroy explores how a growing maze of acronyms, restrictions and visa uncertainty may be undermining Australia's appeal as a study destination.
author: Neil Fitzroy
title_cn: Alphabetti spaghetti and Australia’s international education policy problem

title: Student with gun demands deposit refund from agent
summary_en: A major study abroad agent has told The PIE it was forced to close offices in Pakistan for more than 10 days after a man with a gun demanded a refund of his  tuition fee deposit after being refused a visa to study in the UK.
author: Nicholas Cuthbert
title_cn: Student with gun demands deposit refund from agent

title: Universities Australia warns against growing regulatory burden under Albanese reforms
summary_en: Universities Australia chief executive Luke Sheehy has warned that growing regulation and political intervention is weighing on universities, urging the new tertiary education commission to simplify oversight rather than add to it.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Universities Australia warns against growing regulatory burden under Albanese reforms
